newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - FEB 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - FEB 18.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--As the deadline approaches for tax declarations, Greeks are still confused over how to complete the new E9 real estate declaration which will be used to calculate the government's new real estate tax. Repeated clarifications by the finance ministry have failed to clear the issue. Now, a new information leaflet has been issued.

--The fuss that has erupted over the government's plans to transfer pension funds' to the Bank of Greece has taken on political, rather than economic, tones, indicating a lack of coordination amongst ministers. Unionists warned yesterday they would boycott the government's social dialogue talks if the amendment was not withdrawn.

--The new agreement on shop trading hours has left major supermarket chains out in the cold, with the two biggest - Marinopoulos and Continent - resigning from department store associations. Labour Minister Miltiades Papaiannou said that the new agreement would be implemented soon.
--The government's amendment to transfer pension funds' reserves to the central bank is both a voluntary measure and corrective, National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou says.
--The finance ministry admitted yesterday that its E9 form was difficult and said that as of Monday the tax department would be available to answer any questions by taxpayers.

--The government was optimistic yesterday morning about an end to the five-week teachers' strike but received a slap in the face from the union OLME later in the evening, when it decided to continue for a sixth week. A number of unionists, however, have called for resumption of negotiations with the government on the entire range of demands.

--A new poll shows recent farmers' and teachers' protests taking their toll on the popularity of Agriculture Minister Stephanos Tzoumakas and Education Minister Gerasimos Arsenis. Both come last in preferences, while Culture Minister Evangelos Venizelos (67.4 percent), Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos (65.4 percent) and Public Order Minister George Romeos (63.5 percent) lead the field.

--Left Coalition leader Nikos Constantopoulos is the most popular political party leader with 68.1 percent, leading Prime Minister Costas Simitis (54.7 percent) and Democratic Social Movement leader Dimitris Tsovolas (59.5 percent). Conservative opposition leader Miltiades Evert trails with 25.5 percent.
--Brutal pit bull fights in northern Greece have caused a public outcry: the dogs themselves could cost up to two million drachmas.
--Following the bashing of popular TV gymnast Eleni Petroulaki by her former boyfriend, Olympiakos striker Ilia Ivic, experts say one in three Greek women suffer from domestic violence.

--Reports say that Washington has intervened with Athens and Ankara regarding planned Greek and Turkish military exercises off the Aegean island of Hios to avoid both sides using the same international airspace at the same time.
--Parents have sent an urgent plea to the government to resolve the ongoing teachers' strike which has meant the loss of 126 teaching hours so far.
